A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoSA framework and MoVid dataset. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation benchmarks, component ablations, dataset analyses, and user studies, including Tables 1–13.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds motion-focused evaluations, viewpoint-data ablations, human-animation ablations, and occlusion examples.

M1.justification: The structure–appearance architecture, HADC modules, training objectives, and generation procedures are retained. The added contact-loss gradient discussion explains the existing component without establishing a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: MoVid, HumanVid, and the existing text-to-video, image-to-video, and animation tasks are retained. Appendix E.6 and Figure 18 extend the illustrated test scenarios to additional environmental occlusions, including vegetation and boxes.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds Uni3C alongside the retained Animate Anyone, Champ, and HumanVid comparators. The new motion-metric comparisons in Tables 15–16 use six existing general-video baselines, excluding ModelScope, which remains in the original comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix I substantially expands evaluation with DWPose confidence, tracking-point jerk, Qwen3-VL contact-violation and action-recognition scoring, and motion-plausibility/action-correctness user judgments. Tables 17–18 add training-data and component-removal controls. Previously stated training budgets, resolution, and benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests excluding side-view or back-view training data (Table 17), component ablations for human animation (Table 18), and occlusion case studies (Figure 18). Table 14 extends the existing no-structure versus 2D versus 3D ablation with motion-specific measurements and human judgments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Pose Confidence metric measures pose-estimator output confidence, not statistical uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Retained numerical entries are unchanged, but Tables 14–18 add substantial motion-metric, preference, and ablation results. Table 15 reports MoSA pose confidence of 0.911 and contact violations of 1.08%. The added Uni3C row changes Table 12's FVD leader: 562.7 versus MoSA's unchanged 568.3. Figures 10 and 18 add qualitative results.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a localized gradient derivation through the SDF, VGGT, and MoSA in Equations 11–17. Its Equation 12 covers penetration penalties but omits the nonpenetration attraction branch retained in Equation 10, so it does not fully derive the stated loss.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same claims about structure–appearance decoupling, motion-control components, MoVid, and superior generation performance. Additional evaluations support these existing claims without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 7 acknowledges distorted or blurred fingers, attributes the difficulty to insufficient hand-joint annotations, and proposes denser structural guidance. Appendix E.6 adds a substantive explanation of how mask supervision restricts appearance generation to visible body regions under occlusion.

D1.justification: v3 documents contact-loss backpropagation through VGGT and identifies computation tools and procedures for the new metrics. The front-page project link is removed. The code/data release promise and Appendix D's hardware, hyperparameters, and training budget remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to MV-VTON and self-supervised HDR imaging in Appendix D, while removing Let's Dance and MagCache citations. The related-work narrative and novelty positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged; Uni3C was already cited in v2.

P1.justification: v3 adds a discussion section, occlusion and motion-metric appendix subsections, and a longer contact-loss explanation. Front matter, acknowledgments, and cross-references are updated, and the LLM declaration moves from Appendix I to J. Most existing prose and section ordering are preserved.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation substantially expands with motion-evaluation and ablation Tables 14–18, an expanded wall-squat comparison in Figure 10, and occlusion examples in Figure 18. Table 12 gains a comparator row. Existing diagrams and imagery are retained, with figure renumbering, table relocation, and conference-header layout changes.

improvement.justification: The targeted motion evaluations and ablations provide more direct support for the motion-coherence claims, Uni3C strengthens the comparison, and explicit hand-motion limitations improve transparency. These gains are tempered by sparse protocol details for the added evaluations and Appendix B's incomplete derivation: Equation 12 omits Equation 10's nonpenetration attraction term.
